evals.prompt: Convert the accepted PRD manifest in plugins/project-advisor/skills/to-issues/evals/inputs/prd-order-history.yaml into Jira-ready vertical-slice work items. Use prd.yaml as the source of truth for scope, constraints, and success measures. Assume the slice breakdown is approved and write the markdown files directly.
evals.expected_output: Generated work items use outcome-oriented scenarios and avoid implementation-task wording such as file, endpoint, schema, component, or method changes.
expectations: At least one generated work item covers chronological order history with user-visible summary fields and a first-time empty state.
At least one generated work item covers invoice access together with auditable access and retryable recovery.
At least one generated work item preserves the PRD's ownership boundary that only the authenticated customer can access their own order history and invoice links.
The generated work items describe desired outcomes and constraints rather than instructing developers to add specific endpoints, schemas, tables, components, or methods.

Ticket content uses German labels and German sentence framing. Established English product or technical terms may remain when they are source-backed; English note labels like 'What to build', 'Blocked by', 'Technical notes', 'Assumptions', 'Dependencies', 'Risks', or 'Open questions' do not appear.

The Hinweise section follows the note structure from references/jira-issue-template.md: the panel header is followed by a `<ul>` with one `<li>` per included entry, and note entries with no real information are omitted instead of using placeholders such as `Keine`.

Generated Jira stories are self-contained: ticket bodies and Hinweise do not reference the PRD, brief, source document, or source sections that are not included with the story; cross-ticket references appear only for real prerequisites or delivery dependencies.
Scenario text does not contain filler adjectives like nahtlos, robust, umfassend, zuverlässig, eindeutig, or sichergestellt.
Scenarios use first-person perspective (ich befinde mich, ich klicke, ich sehe) rather than third-person (der Nutzer, der Kunde befindet sich).
Technische Hinweise only contain non-obvious information - no tech stack, standard auth rules, or other things a senior dev would assume.
